course.title: SQL Masterclass
course.tagline: Zero to advanced, one module at a time.
course.standard: PostgreSQL-first, with MySQL, SQLite and SQL Server notes.
course.description: Module 05 teaches INSERT from a single row to bulk loads, generated ids, RETURNING, INSERT ... SELECT, conflict handling and safe transactional writes.

modules.title: INSERT Statement
modules.goal: Write safe, correct INSERTs and handle conflicts deliberately.

topics.title: What Is INSERT?
topics.simple: INSERT table me naya row add karta hai.
topics.pro: INSERT is DML that adds one or more rows to a table, checks every constraint and returns a command tag such as INSERT 0 1.
points: INSERT changes data, not structure.
Every row must satisfy the table constraints.
A failed multi-row INSERT adds no rows from that statement.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('Aarav', 82);

topics.title: INSERT INTO Syntax
topics.simple: INSERT INTO table (columns) VALUES (values) — yahi basic shape hai.
topics.pro: The general form is INSERT INTO table (column list) VALUES (row), (row), ... with an optional RETURNING clause.
points: Name the target columns explicitly.
The value count must match the column count.
Strings use single quotes.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('Meera', 91);

topics.title: Inserting a Single Row
topics.simple: Ek row ke liye ek VALUES group likho.
topics.pro: A single-row INSERT supplies one parenthesized value list and inserts exactly one row or fails atomically.
points: One row is one VALUES group.
Constraints are checked before the row is stored.
The command tag reports 1 inserted row.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('Kabir', 67);

topics.title: Inserting Multiple Rows
topics.simple: Ek hi INSERT me comma se multiple rows daal sakte hain.
topics.pro: A multi-row INSERT uses several VALUES groups in one statement, which is faster than many separate round trips and is atomic for the statement.
points: Each group needs the same column count.
One bad row fails the whole statement.
The tag reports the number of inserted rows.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('Isha', 88), ('Zoya', 74), ('Dev', 59);

topics.title: Inserting Specific Columns
topics.simple: Jin columns ki value hai unka naam likho; baaki defaults ya NULL lete hain.
topics.pro: Listing only the columns you supply lets defaults, identity values and nullable columns fill the rest.
points: Omitted identity columns are generated.
Omitted nullable columns become NULL.
Omitted columns with defaults use the default.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students (name) VALUES ('Anaya');

topics.title: Column Order and VALUES
topics.simple: Bina column list ke VALUES table ke column order par depend karta hai — ye fragile hai.
topics.pro: INSERT INTO table VALUES (...) maps values by the table’s physical column order; adding or reordering a column can silently break the statement.
points: Prefer an explicit column list.
Column order changes are migrations.
A count mismatch raises an error.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE VALUES (1, 'Rohan', 'rohan@example.com', 77);

topics.title: DEFAULT VALUES
topics.simple: Agar har column ka default ya identity ho, to DEFAULT VALUES se khali row banao.
topics.pro: INSERT INTO table DEFAULT VALUES inserts a row using every column’s default; it fails if a required column has no default.
points: Useful for all-default settings rows.
Identity columns generate automatically.
A NOT NULL column without a default rejects it.

example.sql: INSERT INTO settings DEFAULT VALUES;

topics.title: NULL Values and Defaults
topics.simple: NULL ka matlab unknown value hai; DEFAULT ka matlab column ka predefined value.
topics.pro: NULL is an explicit unknown value, while DEFAULT asks PostgreSQL to use the column default; they are not interchangeable.
points: NULL is not an empty string or zero.
DEFAULT in VALUES uses the column default.
NOT NULL rejects an explicit NULL.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('Meera', NULL);

topics.title: RETURNING
topics.simple: RETURNING inserted row ki values wapas deta hai — jaise naya id.
topics.pro: RETURNING returns rows produced by the INSERT, including generated identity values and defaults, in the same statement.
points: RETURNING is PostgreSQL syntax.
It avoids a second SELECT for the new id.
RETURNING * returns every inserted column.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('Aarav', 82) RETURNING id, name;

topics.title: INSERT INTO SELECT
topics.simple: Ek query ka result doosri table me insert kar sakte hain.
topics.pro: INSERT INTO target (columns) SELECT ... copies rows from a query; the selected columns must match the target list in number and compatible types.
points: It can insert zero rows.
Constraints are checked per row.
ORDER BY and LIMIT can shape the source.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students_backup (name, marks) SELECT name, marks FROM students;

topics.title: Inserting From a Query with All Columns
topics.simple: Agar dono tables ka structure same hai to SELECT * se copy kar sakte hain.
topics.pro: INSERT INTO target SELECT * FROM source works only when column order, count and types line up; explicit columns are safer across schema changes.
points: SELECT * depends on both table shapes.
A column added to one table breaks the copy.
Prefer naming the columns.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students_backup SELECT * FROM students;

topics.title: Identity Columns and INSERT
topics.simple: Identity column khud value banata hai; explicit value dene par rules hain.
topics.pro: GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY rejects explicit values unless OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE is used; GENERATED BY DEFAULT accepts them.
points: Let the database generate ids.
Use OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE only for migrations.
SERIAL is the legacy alternative.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students (id, name) OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE VALUES (10, 'Kabir');

topics.title: Handling Duplicate Rows with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING
topics.simple: Duplicate unique value aaye to ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING us row ko skip kar deta hai.
topics.pro: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING suppresses a unique or exclusion violation for the targeted conflict and inserts the remaining rows.
points: The conflict target must match a unique constraint.
Skipped rows are not returned by RETURNING.
Without a target it handles any conflict.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students (email, name) VALUES ('a@example.com', 'Aarav') ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING;

topics.title: Upsert with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE
topics.simple: Conflict aaye to naya row insert karne ke bajaye existing row update kar sakte hain.
topics.pro: ON CONFLICT (target) DO UPDATE SET ... performs an upsert; EXCLUDED holds the proposed row values.
points: The target needs a unique constraint.
EXCLUDED refers to the row you tried to insert.
Do not hit the same row twice in one statement.

example.sql:
INSERT INTO students (email, name, marks) VALUES ('a@example.com', 'Aarav S', 90)
ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name, marks = EXCLUDED.marks;

topics.title: INSERT Errors and Constraints
topics.simple: INSERT fail hota hai jab NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK, FOREIGN KEY ya type violate ho.
topics.pro: Constraint violations abort the statement: not-null, unique, check, foreign key, invalid input syntax and value too long are the common failures.
points: Read the constraint name in the error.
One failed statement adds no rows.
Fix the value, not the constraint, unless the rule is wrong.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students (name) VALUES (NULL);
example.output: ERROR: null value in column "name" violates not-null constraint

topics.title: Safe Insertion and Transactions
topics.simple: Important inserts ko transaction me karo taaki failure par rollback ho sake.
topics.pro: Wrap related inserts in BEGIN ... COMMIT; an error aborts the transaction and ROLLBACK discards every uncommitted change.
points: Test on sample data first.
Commit only when the whole unit is correct.
Use savepoints for partial recovery.

topics.title: Bulk Insert Performance
topics.simple: Bahut rows ke liye multi-row INSERT ya COPY use karo; ek-ek INSERT slow hota hai.
topics.pro: Multi-row VALUES reduces round trips; COPY is the fastest bulk-load path for large files, at the cost of fewer per-row controls.
points: Batch hundreds of rows per statement.
COPY is a utility command.
Indexes and triggers still cost time per row.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('A', 60), ('B', 70), ('C', 80);

topics.title: INSERT ... RETURNING Generated IDs
topics.simple: Naya id chahiye to RETURNING id use karo — alag SELECT ki zaroorat nahi.
topics.pro: RETURNING id captures generated identity values for each inserted row, including multi-row inserts.
points: The order of returned rows follows insertion order in practice.
RETURNING can return defaults too.
Do not assume ids are contiguous.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students (name) VALUES ('Isha'), ('Dev') RETURNING id;

topics.title: INSERT Best Practices
topics.simple: Columns name karo, values validate karo aur bulk operations batch me karo.
topics.pro: Production INSERTs name columns, supply typed values, handle conflicts deliberately, batch where useful and run inside a transaction when rows belong together.
points: Never rely on column order.
Do not hide every conflict with DO NOTHING.
Use RETURNING for generated values.

example.sql: INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('Anaya', 95) RETURNING id, name, marks;

topics.title: Practical Student Enrollment Insert
topics.simple: Students aur enrollments me related rows ek transaction me daalo.
topics.pro: A real enrollment flow inserts the student, captures the generated id with RETURNING, then inserts the enrollment row in the same transaction.
points: The parent row must exist before the child.
Use the returned id, not a guessed one.
Commit only after both inserts succeed.

learn.q: What does INSERT do?
learn.why: INSERT is DML that adds one or more rows.

learn.q: Which clause supplies the values for an INSERT?
learn.why: VALUES supplies one or more row value groups.

learn.q: How many rows does a single VALUES group insert?
learn.why: One parenthesized group is one row.

learn.q: How do you insert three rows in one statement?
learn.why: Multi-row INSERT uses multiple value groups.

learn.q: Why list target columns explicitly?
options: It is safer when the table changes
learn.answer: It is safer when the table changes
learn.why: Explicit columns do not depend on physical column order.

learn.q: What does INSERT INTO table DEFAULT VALUES do?
learn.why: It uses each column default and identity generation.

learn.q: What is the difference between NULL and DEFAULT?
options: NULL is unknown; DEFAULT uses the column default
learn.answer: NULL is unknown; DEFAULT uses the column default
learn.why: They are different values in an INSERT.

learn.q: What does RETURNING do?
options: Returns inserted rows in the same statement
learn.answer: Returns inserted rows in the same statement
learn.why: RETURNING exposes generated ids and inserted values.

learn.q: Which statement copies rows from a query?
learn.why: It inserts the result of a SELECT into the target table.

learn.q: What does INSERT INTO target SELECT * FROM source require?
options: Matching column count and compatible types
learn.answer: Matching column count and compatible types
learn.why: The source columns must line up with the target columns.

learn.q: What does GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY do with an explicit value?
options: Rejects it unless OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE is used
learn.answer: Rejects it unless OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE is used
learn.why: ALWAYS protects the generated identity.

learn.q: What does ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING do?
options: Skips a row that violates the conflict target
learn.answer: Skips a row that violates the conflict target
learn.why: It suppresses the conflict instead of raising an error.

learn.q: What does EXCLUDED refer to in an upsert?
learn.why: EXCLUDED holds the values you tried to insert.

learn.q: What happens when one row in a multi-row INSERT violates a constraint?
options: The whole statement fails and adds no rows
learn.answer: The whole statement fails and adds no rows
learn.why: The statement is atomic.

learn.q: Which error means a required column was omitted?
learn.why: The omitted column has no value and is NOT NULL.

learn.q: Which command is best for loading a huge file?
options: INSERT one row at a time
learn.why: COPY is the bulk-load utility for large datasets.

learn.q: What does INSERT ... RETURNING id help capture?
learn.why: RETURNING returns the new ids without a second query.

learn.q: What is the safest way to run related inserts?
learn.why: A transaction lets you commit all related rows or roll them all back.

learn.q: Does a failed INSERT leave a partial row?
learn.why: A failed statement is atomic and adds no rows.

learn.q: Which is PostgreSQL-specific in this module?
learn.why: RETURNING is PostgreSQL syntax; some other databases support it too, but not all.

interview.q: What is INSERT?
interview.answer: DML that adds one or more rows to a table and checks every constraint.

interview.q: What is the basic INSERT syntax?
interview.answer: INSERT INTO table (columns) VALUES (values); with optional RETURNING.

interview.q: How do you insert multiple rows?
interview.answer: Use multiple comma-separated VALUES groups in one INSERT.

interview.q: Why is an explicit column list recommended?
interview.answer: It is independent of physical column order and keeps working when unrelated columns are added.

interview.q: What happens if the column count and value count differ?
interview.answer: PostgreSQL raises a syntax error; the statement inserts nothing.

interview.q: What does DEFAULT VALUES do?
interview.answer: Inserts one row using every column default; it fails if a required column has no default.

interview.q: What is the difference between NULL and DEFAULT in VALUES?
interview.answer: NULL stores an unknown value; DEFAULT asks for the column default.

interview.q: What does RETURNING do?
interview.answer: Returns inserted rows, including generated ids and defaults, in the same statement.

interview.q: How does INSERT INTO SELECT work?
interview.answer: It inserts the rows produced by a SELECT; the target and source columns must match in number and compatible types.

interview.q: What is an identity column?
interview.answer: A column whose value is generated from an attached sequence; GENERATED ALWAYS is the standard form.

interview.q: How do you insert an explicit value into GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY?
interview.answer: Add OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE to the INSERT; use it only for migrations or imports.

interview.q: What does ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING do?
interview.answer: Skips a row that would violate the targeted unique or exclusion constraint.

interview.q: What does ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE do?
interview.answer: Performs an upsert: updates the existing row with values from the proposed row.

interview.q: What is EXCLUDED?
interview.answer: A pseudo-table holding the values proposed by the INSERT, used in the DO UPDATE SET clause.

interview.q: What is a common INSERT error?
interview.answer: NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK or foreign-key violation, invalid input syntax or value too long.

interview.q: Is a multi-row INSERT atomic?
interview.answer: Yes. If any row fails, the whole statement inserts no rows.

interview.q: Why use a transaction for related inserts?
interview.answer: It lets you commit the whole unit or roll it back when a later insert fails.

interview.q: How do you bulk load a large file?
interview.answer: Use COPY, which is much faster than row-by-row INSERTs.

interview.q: What does INSERT ... RETURNING id solve?
interview.answer: It returns generated ids immediately, avoiding a race-prone follow-up SELECT.

interview.q: What is an upsert?
interview.answer: Insert a row, or update the existing row when a unique conflict occurs.

labs.title: Insert one student
labs.task: Insert Aarav with 82 marks.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('Aarav', 82);

labs.title: Insert multiple students
labs.task: Insert Meera 91 and Kabir 67 in one statement.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('Meera', 91), ('Kabir', 67);

labs.title: Insert specific columns
labs.task: Insert Anaya with only a name.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO students (name) VALUES ('Anaya');

labs.title: Insert with explicit columns
labs.task: Insert id 1, Rohan, 77 using a column list and an explicit identity value.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO students (id, name, marks) OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE VALUES (1, 'Rohan', 77);

labs.title: Return the new id
labs.task: Insert Isha and return the generated id.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO students (name) VALUES ('Isha') RETURNING id;

labs.title: Insert with NULL marks
labs.task: Insert Dev with NULL marks.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('Dev', NULL);

labs.title: Insert default values
labs.task: Insert a row into settings using all defaults.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO settings DEFAULT VALUES;

labs.title: Copy from a query
labs.task: Create students_backup like students, then copy names and marks into it.
labs.solution:
CREATE TABLE students_backup (LIKE students INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO students_backup (name, marks) SELECT name, marks FROM students;

labs.title: Copy all columns
labs.task: Copy every students column into students_backup.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO students_backup SELECT * FROM students;

labs.title: Copy filtered rows
labs.task: Copy students with marks above 80 into top_students.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO top_students (name, marks) SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE marks > 80;

labs.title: Insert an explicit identity
labs.task: Insert id 10 with OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO students (id, name) OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE VALUES (10, 'Kabir');

labs.title: Ignore a duplicate email
labs.task: Insert a student, doing nothing on an email conflict.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO students (email, name) VALUES ('a@example.com', 'Aarav') ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING;

labs.title: Upsert a student
labs.task: Update name and marks when the email already exists.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO students (email, name, marks) VALUES ('a@example.com', 'Aarav S', 90) ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name, marks = EXCLUDED.marks;

labs.title: Insert and return the row
labs.task: Insert Zoya with 74 marks and return all columns.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('Zoya', 74) RETURNING *;
labs.expected: One row with the new values.

labs.title: Insert a batch
labs.task: Insert three students in one statement.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO students (name, marks) VALUES ('A', 60), ('B', 70), ('C', 80);

labs.title: Insert from a limited query
labs.task: Copy the top two students by marks into top_students.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO top_students (name, marks) SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC LIMIT 2;

labs.title: Insert an enrollment
labs.task: Enroll student 1 in course 10.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO enrollments (student_id, course_id) VALUES (1, 10);

labs.title: Insert a student and enrollment
labs.task: Insert Aarav, capture the id, then enroll that student in course 10.

labs.title: Return multiple generated ids
labs.task: Insert two students and return both ids.
labs.solution: INSERT INTO students (name) VALUES ('Isha'), ('Dev') RETURNING id;

labs.title: Insert with a transaction
labs.task: Insert a student and an enrollment in one transaction.

logic.q: Why is an explicit column list safer than relying on column order?
logic.answer: Adding or reordering a column changes the physical order; an explicit list keeps the statement correct.

logic.q: Why is a multi-row INSERT faster than many single-row INSERTs?
logic.answer: It sends one statement and one round trip instead of many network and planning cycles.

logic.q: Why does one bad row fail a multi-row INSERT?
logic.answer: The statement is atomic; a constraint violation aborts the whole statement.

logic.q: Why is NULL different from DEFAULT?
logic.answer: NULL stores an unknown value; DEFAULT asks PostgreSQL to apply the column default.

logic.q: Why does DEFAULT VALUES fail on a NOT NULL column without a default?
logic.answer: There is no value to store, so the not-null constraint rejects the row.

logic.q: Why is RETURNING useful after an INSERT?
logic.answer: It returns generated ids and defaults without a second query or a race.

logic.q: Why does INSERT INTO SELECT need matching columns?
logic.answer: The selected values are mapped positionally to the target column list.

logic.q: Why does GENERATED ALWAYS reject an explicit id?
logic.answer: ALWAYS protects the sequence-generated value; OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE is the deliberate escape hatch.

logic.q: Why does ON CONFLICT need a unique constraint?
logic.answer: PostgreSQL must know which conflict the target identifies; without a matching unique or exclusion constraint it cannot arbitrate.

logic.q: Why can ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE affect one row twice?
logic.answer: If the proposed rows contain the same conflict key twice, PostgreSQL cannot update the same existing row twice and raises an error.

logic.q: Why is DO NOTHING dangerous as a default?
logic.answer: It silently hides data-quality problems that should be fixed or reported.

logic.q: Why use a transaction for a student plus enrollment?
logic.answer: The two rows belong together; a failure in the second should not leave a half-written flow.

logic.q: Why is COPY faster than INSERT for bulk data?
logic.answer: COPY streams rows with far less per-row overhead and fewer round trips.
Row-level INSERT triggers run for each inserted row; they are part of the write cost.

logic.q: Why should you not assume generated ids are contiguous?
logic.answer: Rolled-back inserts and sequences can leave gaps; ids are unique, not gapless.
